blocks.text: 我们推出 SWE-2 Flash，这是一款完全在美国打造的编程模型，在低成本、高速度的前提下，把智能水平推向了新高度。我们在训练配方中首次于强化学习之前加入了一个中期训练阶段。相比基座模型 Thinking Machines 的 Inkling-Small，这一改动带来了显著提升：Terminal-Bench 4.0 从 0.9% 提升到 20.0%，FrontierCode 2.0 从 3.2% 提升到 24.0%。

blocks.text: 训练

inlines.text: 训练

blocks.text: 我们首先在 Inkling-Small 之上进行大规模中期训练。该模型总参数 276B，激活参数 12B。一个关键挑战是确定合适的数据配比：纳入哪些来源，以及各占多大比例。为指导这些决策，我们整理了一个高质量的留出编程数据集，用来反映模型在真实软件工程场景中的智能水平。

inlines.text: 我们首先在

blocks.text: 随后，我们用 token 效率曲线来评估不同数据源，找出最有效的配比。我们从一次基线训练开始，测量每种候选数据配比需要多少 token 才能达到与基线相同的验证损失。把这一 token 数量的比值画在 y 轴、基线 token 数画在 x 轴，就能直接比较不同配比的训练效率。

blocks.text: 我们反复调整中期训练数据的构成，最终确定了一个由数万亿 token 组成的数据集，涵盖高质量科学文章、博客、代码及其他来源。训练分三个阶段进行，让模型在训练后期才接触到最稀缺、质量最高的数据。在每个阶段中，留出验证损失都以稳定的对数线性速率改善。

blocks.text: 中期训练阶段之后，我们进行了大规模强化学习。虽然我们对 SWE-2 的强化学习配方做了一些调整，但大部分提升来自质量更高、多样性更丰富的强化学习任务。

inlines.text: 中期训练阶段之后，我们进行了大规模强化学习。虽然我们对 SWE-2 的强化学习配方做了一些调整，但大部分提升来自质量更高、多样性更丰富的强化学习任务。

blocks.text: 在质量方面，我们仔细审查了任务的指令、环境配置和验证器。在多样性方面，我们设计了几种新的任务类型，覆盖的能力范围远超以往，以培养 Devin 实际工作所需的通用推理和问题解决能力。用这些数据训练后，我们测得的几乎每一项基准都取得了显著提升。

blocks.text: 起源与网络安全

inlines.text: 起源与网络安全

blocks.text: 对于敏感、关键任务型的工作，客户需要的不仅仅是一个藏在 API 背后的强大模型。随着网络安全逐渐成为一大主要应用场景，风险也随之升高。企业和政府需要可观测性，以便在自己的基础设施上（包括本地部署）托管和控制部署。学术界和产业界的研究人员则需要研究模型的行为方式，以及模型可能被如何滥用。

inlines.text: 对于敏感、关键任务型的工作，客户需要的不仅仅是一个藏在 API 背后的强大模型。随着网络安全逐渐成为一大主要应用场景，风险也随之升高。企业和政府需要可观测性，以便在自己的基础设施上（包括本地部署）托管和控制部署。学术界和产业界的研究人员则需要研究模型的行为方式，以及模型可能被如何滥用。

blocks.text: SWE-2 Flash 的目标之一，是为行业合作伙伴和研究人员提供一个选项：既能透明地访问模型权重，又能对模型进行微调，并在敏感环境中运行。为了帮助防御方，我们在训练中重点针对网络安全工作，将模型的 ExploitBench 得分从 11.3% 提升到 34.8%。这些能力同样可能被恶意攻击者利用，近期网络攻击激增就是明证，因此我们暂不公开权重。作为兼顾透明度与安全性的潜在方案，我们正在制定一项计划，与可信的行业合作伙伴和研究实验室安全地共享权重。更多细节将在几周后公布。

blocks.text: We’re introducing SWE-2 Flash, a fully American coding model that sets a new bar for intelligence at low cost and high speed. For the first time, we added a mid-training stage before reinforcement learning in our recipe. This results in significant gains over the base model, Inkling-Small from Thinking Machines, improving Terminal-Bench 4.0 from 0.9% to 20.0% and FrontierCode 2.0 from 3.2% to 24.0%.

blocks.text: On leading evals, SWE-2 Flash outperforms all American open-weight models, even models that are 3x larger. To balance transparent access and cyber risks, we are building a program to securely share the weights with industry partners and researchers.

Today, smaller models are increasingly able to handle a significant portion of the work that software agents do, such as automations, code review, feature development, and updating documentation.

blocks.text: Training

inlines.text: Training

blocks.text: We began with a large-scale mid-training stage on top of Inkling-Small, a model with 276B total and 12B active parameters. A key challenge was determining the right data mix: which sources to include, and in what proportions. To guide these decisions, we curated a high-quality held-out coding dataset that reflects model intelligence in real-world software engineering scenarios.

inlines.text: We began with a large-scale mid-training stage on top of
Inkling-Small

, a model with 276B total and 12B active parameters. A key challenge was determining the right data mix: which sources to include, and in what proportions. To guide these decisions, we curated a high-quality held-out coding dataset that reflects model intelligence in real-world software engineering scenarios.

blocks.text: We then used token efficiency plots to evaluate different data sources and identify the most effective mixtures. Starting with a baseline training run, we measured how many tokens each candidate data mix needed to reach the same validation loss as the baseline. By plotting the ratio of these token counts on the y-axis and baseline tokens on the x-axis, we could directly compare the training efficiency of different mixtures.

By plotting the ratio of these token counts on the y-axis and baseline tokens on the x-axis, we could directly compare the training efficiency of different mixtures.

blocks.text: We iterated on the composition of our mid-training data and converged on a dataset composed of a few trillion tokens of high-quality scientific articles, blogs, code, and other sources. Training proceeded in three stages, so that the model would see the scarcest, highest-quality data later in training. Throughout each stage, held-out validation loss improved at a stable log-linear rate.

blocks.text: We followed the mid-training phase with large-scale reinforcement learning. While we made some tweaks to our RL recipe from SWE-2, most of the improvements came from the much higher quality and diversity of our RL tasks.

inlines.text: We followed the mid-training phase with large-scale reinforcement learning. While we made some tweaks to our RL recipe from SWE-2, most of the improvements came from the much higher quality and diversity of our RL tasks.

blocks.text: On quality, we carefully audited the instructions, environment setup, and verifiers for our tasks. On diversity, we curated several new task types covering a far wider range of capabilities than before, to build the general reasoning and problem-solving skills that real work in Devin demands. Training on this data led to significant improvements on nearly every benchmark we measured.

blocks.text: Origins & Cyber

inlines.text: Origins & Cyber

blocks.text: For sensitive, mission-critical work, customers need more than a capable model behind an API. As cybersecurity grows into a major use case, the stakes get even higher. Enterprises and governments need observability to host and control deployments on their own infrastructure, including on-prem. Researchers in academia and industry need to study how models behave and how they can be misused.

inlines.text: For sensitive, mission-critical work, customers need more than a capable model behind an API. As cybersecurity grows into a major use case, the stakes get even higher. Enterprises and governments need observability to host and control deployments on their own infrastructure, including on-prem. Researchers in academia and industry need to study how models behave and how they can be misused.

blocks.text: One of our goals with SWE-2 Flash is to provide an option to industry partners and researchers that allows transparent access to weights along with the ability to fine-tune and run it in sensitive environments. To help defenders, we targeted cybersecurity work in our training, raising the model’s ExploitBench score from 11.3% to 34.8%. These same capabilities can also be used by malicious attackers, as demonstrated by a recent surge in cyber attacks, so we are not sharing the weights publicly yet. As a potential solution that balances both transparency and safety, we are building a program to securely share the weights with trusted industry partners and research labs. More on this in a few weeks.
